segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yeah, so I need a gut check on Northline. They approved 47 seats at $68 per user, annual, net 30, and they want the agreement extended through January 31, 2027.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: That lines up with the pricing sheet. Any services on it?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Just the standard onboarding package, $3,200 one-time. Go-live target is February 3. Their finance lead asked that the first invoice not go out until February 1.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Okay, that’s all normal. What’s the blocker?

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: The blocker is getting the actual proposal out. To extend the agreement I have to put the same customer name, billing address, 47 seats, $68 rate, contract end date, invoice timing, and onboarding fee into the pricing sheet, then the quote tool, then the approval portal, then the billing tool, then the order form generator, and then the e-sign packet. None of them carry the fields over. I did the first pass yesterday afternoon, deal desk asked for the invoice date added, and now I’m retyping the same seven fields everywhere again. It’s like six hours across two days for a renewal that is already verbally approved.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Yeah, that’s painful. For Northline specifically, I can review the numbers before you send so we don’t get another bounce.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Please. I’ve got the order form showing $38,352 annual subscription, plus $3,200 onboarding, total $41,552 before tax.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: That math is right. Make sure the term says February 1, 2026 through January 31, 2027, not the go-live date.

segments.speaker: Maya
segments.text: Yep, good catch. Their procurement person is out Friday, so I’m trying to get it to them by 2 p.m. today.

segments.speaker: Jordan
segments.text: Send me the draft when it’s ready. I’ll turn it in fifteen minutes.
